data.name: Tools_Note
data.value: Windows' own repair tools, run only when you press a button. SFC checks and repairs the protected system files (5-15 minutes); the DISM check looks at the component store SFC repairs from; the DISM repair fixes that store and may download from Windows Update (it cannot be stopped half-way). Settings this page does not change itself open in Windows' own windows.

data.name: Tools_Result_Repaired
data.value: Finished: problems were found and repaired.

data.name: Tools_Result_Damaged

data.name: Tools_Result_Unknown

data.name: Gaming_Note
data.value: The Windows power plan, switched here and reversible, and the state of Game Mode and hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling, changed in Windows' own settings. GPU overclocking and undervolting are on the Overclock & undervolt page; an FPS overlay is not offered.

data.name: Bench_Note
data.value: Benchmarks measure speed. They give numbers only - no score, no pass or fail - and are not a health test. Close other programs first. Tick several and run them one after another, or run one on its own. A single run is saved as a report of its own and a queue as one report (Reports page); the latest result of each is also added to the next test report.

data.name: Bench_Invalid_Duration

data.name: Tuning_Note
data.value: GPU overclock, undervolt, power limit and fan through NVIDIA's own management library (NVML). Every setting is volatile: a restart or a driver reset puts the card back to stock. Values outside the driver's ranges are refused.

data.name: Tuning_Manual_Note
data.value: NVIDIA's public interface does not set a voltage directly. An undervolt is a positive core offset together with a clock cap: the offset lifts the voltage/frequency curve, the cap keeps the clock where it was, so the card reaches that clock at a lower voltage. An overclock is a higher cap (or no cap) with an offset.

data.name: Tuning_Hint_CoreOffset
data.value: Shifts the whole voltage/frequency curve; + raises the clock at every voltage.

data.name: Tuning_Hint_MemoryOffset
data.value: In the unit NVML reports the memory clock in.

data.name: Tuning_Hint_MaxClock
data.value: Unchecked: no cap (the driver's own boost).

data.name: Tuning_Hint_Fan
data.value: Unchecked: automatic fan. A fixed speed stays until you set it back.

data.name: Tuning_Auto_Note
data.value: Automatic undervolt measures the card at stock under a verified GPU load, then raises the offset step by step at the same clock until it computes wrongly, the driver resets, or the clock drops; it backs off a margin and confirms with a long run. Automatic overclock starts from the undervolt and raises the clock cap, then the memory offset, while the card stays correct, gets faster and draws no more power than at stock. A result is saved as a profile only when the measurements beat stock. Takes about 10–25 minutes; the screen may flicker or go black for a moment if the driver resets. Close games and save your work first.

data.name: Tuning_Profiles_Note
data.value: A profile is only offered on the card it was made on. Applying it lasts until the next restart.

data.name: Tuning_Memory_Note
data.value: XMP, DOCP and EXPO are picked by the BIOS while it trains the memory at power-on; Windows has no standard interface to switch them, and no board maker publishes one for desktop boards. It is changed in BIOS setup, which this button restarts straight into (UEFI machines).

data.name: Tuning_Applied
data.value: Applied. The driver accepted every setting.

data.name: Tuning_ResetDone
data.value: The card is back to stock.

data.name: Tuning_ConfirmAuto
data.value: The automatic search loads the graphics card fully for about 10–25 minutes and deliberately pushes it until it becomes unstable. The screen may go black for a moment, and in rare cases the PC may freeze and need a restart (the card is then back at stock). Close games and save your work. Start?

data.name: Tuning_ConfirmApplyFound
data.value: Profile “{0}” ({1}) was saved. Apply it now?

data.name: Tuning_ConfirmFirmware
data.value: The PC restarts now, straight into BIOS setup. Save your work first. Continue?

data.name: Tuning_OtherGpus
data.value: Not tunable here yet: {0}. AMD cards need AMD's ADLX library and Intel Arc cards Intel's IGCL; neither is built in.

data.name: Tuning_Recovered
data.value: An automatic GPU tuning run did not finish (it was trying {0}, started {1}) – the PC probably froze or restarted. The card has been put back to stock.

data.name: Tuning_RecoveredNoReset
data.value: An automatic GPU tuning run did not finish (it was trying {0}, started {1}). The card could not be reset from here; restart the PC to be sure it runs at stock.

data.name: Tuning_Unavailable_NoNvidia
data.value: No NVIDIA graphics card with its driver was found. GPU tuning currently works on NVIDIA cards only.

data.name: Tuning_Unavailable_Nvml

data.name: Tuning_Out_StockUnstable
data.value: The card already made errors at stock settings. It was not tuned – run the GPU tests first.

data.name: Tuning_Out_NoTelemetry
data.value: The driver does not report this card's clock or power, so a result could not be measured.

data.name: Tuning_Out_NoCoreOffset
data.value: This card or driver has no core offset control.

data.name: Tuning_Out_ConfirmFailed
data.value: No setting passed the long confirmation run. Nothing was saved.

data.name: Tuning_Out_SlowerThanStock
data.value: The stable setting ran slower than stock, so it was not kept.

data.name: Tuning_Out_UndervoltFound
data.value: Undervolt found: same clock and performance as stock with less power or heat.

data.name: Tuning_Out_NoSaving
data.value: A stable offset was found, but it did not measurably lower power or temperature, so it was not kept.

data.name: Tuning_Out_NoStableOffset
data.value: Even the first offset step was unstable; this card has no undervolt margin at its stock clock.

data.name: Tuning_Out_OverclockFound
data.value: Overclock found: measurably faster than stock without drawing more power.

data.name: Tuning_Out_NoGain
data.value: The stable setting was not measurably faster than stock, so it was not kept.

data.name: Tuning_Out_ApplyRefused
data.value: The driver refused a setting the search needs

data.name: Tuning_Out_NoResult
data.value: The search ended without a result.

data.name: Tuning_Out_Cancelled

data.name: Tuning_Curve_None
data.value: This card's curve has not been measured yet. “Measure the curve” loads the card for about a minute and a half and records, at each clock, the voltage the card really chooses.

data.name: Tuning_Curve_Empty

data.name: Tuning_Curve_LegendTuned
data.value: With the settings on the form

data.name: Tuning_Curve_Hint
data.value: As in Afterburner: grab a yellow point and drag it up or down to put that voltage on that clock, flat above it (an undervolt). Drag the dotted cap line on its own; Ctrl+drag moves the whole curve. Changes stay on the form until you press Apply. NVIDIA's public interface cannot move single points on their own.

data.name: Tuning_Curve_Estimate
data.value: Estimate from the measured points: at {0} about {1} (stock: {2})

data.name: Tuning_Curve_EstimateAboveStock
data.value: Estimate from the measured points: at {0} about {1} (stock does not reach this clock)

data.name: Tuning_Curve_OutOfRange
data.value: This setting is outside the measured curve; its voltage is not estimated.

data.name: Tuning_Curve_Step
data.value: Measuring the curve: point {0} of {1} · cap {2}

data.name: Tuning_Curve_Done
data.value: The curve was measured and saved. The card is back to stock.

data.name: Tuning_ConfirmCurve
data.value: Measuring the curve loads the graphics card for about a minute and a half and caps its clock step by step. The card's current settings are removed, and at the end it is back at stock. Start?

data.name: Tuning_Curve_ApplyRefused
data.value: The driver refused the clock cap; the curve cannot be measured

data.name: Tuning_Curve_Lost
data.value: The driver reset during the scan. The card is back to stock.

data.name: Tuning_Curve_NoVoltage
data.value: The card's core voltage sensor could not be read, so the curve cannot be measured.

data.name: Tuning_Curve_TooFew
data.value: The card did not reach enough distinct clocks (most likely power or temperature limited); no curve was saved.

data.name: Tuning_AutoUndervolt_Desc
data.value: Stock performance at a lower voltage; kept only when power or temperature measurably drops.

data.name: Tuning_AutoOverclock_Desc
data.value: Starts from the undervolt and raises the core and memory clocks; kept only when the measured score rises.

data.name: Overlay_Note
data.value: A small always-on-top panel with GPU and CPU temperatures, load, clocks and power, RAM and network, and a one-minute load and temperature trend. The mouse passes through it. It shows over games in borderless or windowed mode, not in exclusive full screen. Frame rate (FPS) is not shown: the app does not measure it.
